description: A pure CALCULATION node — combine TWO matrices into one: A+B, A−B, A·B (matrix product), A∘B (element-wise ×) or A/B. Element-wise ops BROADCAST, so a scalar or an N×1 column combines with an N×2 vector list. Draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: two matrices as JSON in, one matrix as JSON out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

INPUTS: wire a matrix into valin-a and valin-b — Grid Geometry's `val-matrix` (a bare rows×cols 2D array `[[…],…]`), another Matrix / Vector node's output, or a POINT LIST such as Space Geometry's / Polygon's `val-points` (an N×2 list IS an N-row matrix — that is how this reaches real geometry). A val-grid `{ "values": [[…]] }` is accepted too. A bare NUMBER wired in (e.g. an Input Properties slider) is read as a 1×1 matrix so it broadcasts.

OPERATIONS:
• Add (A+B) / Subtract (A−B) — element-wise.
• Multiply (A·B) — the MATRIX PRODUCT (rows of A dotted with columns of B). Requires A's cols = B's rows; the result is A.rows × B.cols. Order matters — A·B ≠ B·A. NOT broadcast.
• Multiply element-wise (A∘B) — the Hadamard product, cell-by-cell.
• Divide (A/B) — element-wise. Division by ≈0 yields 0 rather than Infinity, so one degenerate cell can't poison the whole list.

BROADCASTING (all element-wise ops): a dimension must MATCH or be 1, in which case it stretches. So N×2 with 1×1 scales every component by a scalar, and N×2 with N×1 applies a PER-ROW scalar (exactly the miter-vector divide B / (1 + n̂·n̂ₚ)).

Incompatible shapes, a ragged matrix, or empty input return an EMPTY matrix — check `val-rows` > 0.

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` — the result; plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. Transpose → Matrix Operations (A·B) gives AᵀA, and feeding that to Inverse builds the least-squares normal equations x = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀb. An N×2 result can be wired straight into a Polygon node's `valin-points` to DRAW it. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
